### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | High — international cognitive-science authorship |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium — accepts non-Western data within cognitive-science empirical framework |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Medium-High — neurodiversity, bilingualism, cross-cultural cognition published |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Experimental cognitive psychology — child/animal learning (1,362), reading/literacy (852), bilingualism/language (817), visual perception (555), moral judgment (533), math cognition (506), multisensory integration (479) per OpenAlex |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (soft)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts judged by **scientific quality, degree of innovation, and unambiguous theoretical advance**. Argument soundness + empirical motivation prioritized over methodological orthodoxy. Less methodologically dogmatic than some venues.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Manuscripts without theoretical advance face desk reject; methodological reviewers expect rigorous controls but accept innovative paradigms.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Core method — controlled cognitive experiments |
| Qualitative interviews | 1 | Rare |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 4 | Theoretical analysis welcomed (community evidence: Elsevier author guide 2026-05) |
| Mixed methods | 2 | Accepted with quantitative dominance |
| Meta-analysis | 4 | Welcomed |
| Computational modeling | 5 | Distinctive Cognition strength |

| Aspect | Detail |

| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | 2 — third-person scholarly register; first-person occasional |
| **Expected density** | Low |
| **Writing style notes** | Formal academic register; cognitive-psychology vocabulary; long word allowance compared to brief-report journals; theoretical-empirical balance expected |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers drawn primarily from the experimental cognitive psychology community — international faculty with strong methodological depth in language, perception, memory, attention, learning, and computational cognition. Single-blind review per Elsevier default. Common reviewer demands: "Unambiguous theoretical advance?", "Innovation beyond replication?", "Argument soundness?". Reviewers tolerant of paradigm diversity if theoretical contribution is clear.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Experimental cognitive psychology | https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/cognition |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Medium — strong methodological depth |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (strong) — quantitative experimental work is the journal's center of gravity |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | International cognitive-psychology programs |

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Manuscripts without unambiguous theoretical advance (community evidence: Cognition editorial standard 2026-05)
- Pure replication studies without theoretical contribution
- Autoethnography or pure qualitative submissions
- AI-generated images per Elsevier policy
- Failure to disclose AI use

### Soft Tax

Low for cognitive-experimental tradition authors. Moderate for theoretical-only work — requires linking theory to empirical motivation. APC $3,710 USD for OA option (community evidence: Elsevier 2026-05); subscription path $0 but 24-month AAM embargo. Long word allowance is a relative advantage compared to brief-report journals.

### Best Suited For

- Experimental cognitive psychology empirical studies
- Language, bilingualism, reading, literacy development research
- Visual perception, multisensory integration, attention work
- Moral and emotional judgment cognitive studies
- Computational cognitive modeling
- Theoretical-cognitive analysis with empirical motivation
- Long-form cognitive-experimental papers with multiple studies

### Not Recommended For

- Pure replication studies without theoretical advance
- Autoethnography or first-person work
- Pure clinical or applied psychology (consider JCCP, J Applied Psych)
- Submissions framed for non-cognitive-science audiences
- Authors needing rapid OA visibility (24-month AAM embargo on subscription path)

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Journal of Experimental Psychology General](../psychology/journal-of-experimental-psychology-general.md) | APA flagship; closest cognitive-experimental scope; no AAM embargo |
| 2 | [Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience](./journal-of-cognitive-neuroscience.md) | If the work has neuroscience grounding; MIT Press; preregistered Reports option |
| 3 | [Trends in Cognitive Sciences](./trends-in-cognitive-sciences.md) | If the work is reframed as theoretical synthesis (pre-submission proposal track) |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a top general-psychology venue as "too cognitive / too experimental," Cognition is often a better fit because: it specializes in experimental cognitive psychology with deep reviewer-pool expertise; theoretical advance is the editorial standard rather than broad-significance generalization; and long word allowance accommodates multi-study cognitive programs.
